title: Noor and the Promise
premise: Ulyana Galloway, a ghostwriter who rebuilt her life in careful, invisible increments after a public scandal destroyed her name, is hired to secretly write the memoirs of Vivienne Marsh—a rival whose success was built on a story Ulyana once told her in confidence. Cornered into bringing a date to the Marsh family reunion to keep up her cover, she recruits Noor Haddad, a warm, perceptive archivist who begins seeing through every layer of her disguise. As the deadline for the memoir approaches and Vivienne grows suspicious, Ulyana must decide whether to expose the theft of her own story and lose everything again, or stay silent and lose Noor, the one person who loves the woman beneath the ghost. In the end, Ulyana publishes the truth under her own name, forfeits the career that saved her, and chooses Noor—discovering that identity isn't what survived, but what she dares to claim.
about_author: Ansel Vane is the pen name of a former publishing insider who spent years writing other people's truths before claiming a voice of their own. They live quietly by the sea, where they write stories about people learning to be seen.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Contract
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She signs the contract to ghostwrite Vivienne Marsh's memoirs, telling herself it's just another job—until she reads the outline and recognizes her own stolen history in Chapter One. The beat is quiet dread: the past has teeth, and she's agreed to feed it.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Small Steps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, flashback-woven. We learn how a plagiarized manuscript and a very public humiliation drove her into ghostwriting anonymity, and how she measures safety now: rented flat, no byline, no attachments. The beat is fragile equilibrium about to be disturbed.

chapters.title: An Invitation with Thorns
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Vivienne summons Ulyana to help prepare for the Marsh family reunion at Thornfield House—and casually announces Ulyana must bring a partner, since 'single' doesn't fit the polished narrative she wants. The beat is gilded menace disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Panicking, she remembers Noor Haddad, the patient archivist who helped her research a previous book and who owes her a favor. She asks for one fake weekend. Noor agrees with unsettling ease—and asks one question Ulyana can't answer honestly. The beat is nervous spark.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Over coffee, they build their fake relationship: how they met, first kiss, inside jokes. Noor watches Ulyana lie fluently about small things and wonders what big things she's hiding. The beat is intimacy growing in the cracks of a performance.

chapters.title: Thornfield House
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Arrival at the reunion: marble halls, Vivienne's adoring family, and Ulyana performing happiness on Noor's arm while cataloguing exits. The beat is claustrophobic charm—she's playing a role inside someone else's house again.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Between toasts and interrogations from Vivienne's sharp-eyed aunt, the fake couple's chemistry stops being fake; a dance on the terrace ends an inch from a real kiss. The beat is dangerous warmth—Noor realizes he doesn't want the act to end.

chapters.title: The Kiss That Wasn't Scripted
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The kiss happens anyway, and Ulyana flees to her room, terrified—not of exposure, but of wanting something real enough to lose. The beat is panic and longing tangled together.

chapters.title: What Vivienne Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, late night. Snooping for evidence of the plagiarism, she finds Vivienne's locked study and the original letter Ulyana wrote ten years ago—the confession that became Vivienne's origin story. The beat is cold confirmation: this was never paranoia.

chapters.title: Sunday Morning Lies
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor catches Ulyana returning from the study at dawn and confronts her gently; she lies badly, and he lets her, hurt but unwilling to push. The beat is the first real fracture between them.

chapters.title: Deadline Pressure
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Back in London, Vivienne tightens the screws: the memoir must be finished in six weeks, and she hints she knows Ulyana is 'researching more than the book.' The beat is the trap closing—Vivienne suspects and enjoys it.

chapters.title: Almost Honest
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A rain-soaked evening with Noor nearly becomes full confession; instead she tells him a half-truth about a rival and a stolen story, omitting her own name. He sees the omission clearly. The beat is love meeting the limits of trust.

chapters.title: The Archive Box
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Working in his archive, Noor finds a rejected manuscript submission from ten years ago bearing Ulyana's real name—and matches it, line for line, to Vivienne's celebrated debut. The beat is devastating clarity: he now knows exactly who she is and what was taken.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Instead of confronting her, Noor waits, holding the truth like something breakable, watching Ulyana shrink smaller under Vivienne's demands. The beat is agonizing tenderness—he loves her and cannot yet say why he's grieving.

chapters.title: Blackmail in Silk
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV. Vivienne reveals she's known Ulyana's identity all along and offers a devil's bargain: finish the memoir beautifully and stay anonymous forever, or be exposed as a disgraced plagiarist again—with Noor collateral damage. The beat is open villainy; the mask comes off.

chapters.title: The Choice
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Shattered, Ulyana weighs survival against truth: the career that rebuilt her versus the self she buried, and Noor, who would stand beside either version. The beat is the novel's dark night—she drafts two endings, one for the memoir, one for herself.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She tells Noor everything on the empty shore near his archive—her name, the theft, the bargain. He answers not with absolution but with fury on her behalf: 'You were robbed, and you apologized for bleeding.' The beat is catharsis; love survives honesty.

chapters.title: Chapter One, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana writes the memoir's final chapter as the truth: her story, her name, submitted simultaneously to Vivienne and to a literary editor who once believed in her. The beat is defiant calm—she signs her own work for the first time in a decade.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Thornfield
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax. At a launch event for the memoir, Vivienne publicly accuses Ulyana of fabrication—but Noor produces the archived original manuscript, dated and witnessed, and Vivienne's own family turns. The beat is explosive vindication with real cost.

chapters.title: Ashes and Bylines
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The fallout: Vivienne's empire cracks, Ulyana's exposé goes viral, and offers flood in—but so does the old terror of visibility. She almost retreats. The beat is victory shadowed by fear; being seen still feels like danger.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor finds Ulyana packing to disappear again and makes her a promise: he will love the visible woman, the bylined woman, the frightened woman—all of her, out loud, in daylight. The beat is the emotional climax resolved in quiet certainty.

chapters.title: Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue. A year later, Ulyana's own memoir launches—dedicated to 'the archivist who reads carefully.' At the signing table, Noor waits in line with a copy, and she signs it with her real name and a kiss. The beat is earned joy: identity reclaimed, love chosen, nothing hidden.
